question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, egress 205.188.204.187
request.body: one keyless tools/call of microsoft_docs_search, query "Azure Functions durable orchestration", sent five times, all answering 200: to the endpoint with no maxTokenBudget, then maxTokenBudget=2000, 200, 0 and notanumber

decoded.the-vendor-claim: the vendor's repository README, under Token Budget Control, reads "To manage token usage and control costs, you can append the maxTokenBudget query parameter to the MCP endpoint URL. This parameter limits the token count in search tool responses by truncating the content to meet your specified budget", and marks the feature experimental
decoded.measured-true-two-byte-counts: same query, one pass at 12:22:33Z, reported as CONTENT bytes (the length of result.content[0].text) with the raw event-stream response length beside it, because the two differ and only the first is the documentation delivered: no parameter 28958 content / 59003 raw; maxTokenBudget=2000 12675 / 26155; maxTokenBudget=200 2341 / 5310. The parameter works as documented for an anonymous caller. The head first filed on pull request #205 published only the content figures under a command that counted raw bytes, which a reviewer caught; the command now decodes the content field and counts its UTF-8 bytes, and both numbers are here so either is checkable
decoded.the-result-count-does-not-change: ten results at every budget, including at 200. The parameter truncates each chunk's content; it does not return fewer complete results. An agent budgeting its context gets ten stubs rather than two whole articles and cannot choose the other trade. No vendor page read on this date says which way it truncates
decoded.invalid-values-are-ignored-silently: maxTokenBudget=0 and maxTokenBudget=notanumber both returned 28958 content bytes and 59003 raw bytes, byte-for-byte the unbudgeted response, with no error and no warning. A typo in the value, or presumably in the parameter name, delivers the full response to a caller who believes it is capped
decoded.two-readings: the five requests were sent once at about 12:15Z and again at 12:22:33Z, when the raw byte counts were added; every figure was identical across the two, so the search index behind them did not move in seven minutes. That is a control for this record's own window and says nothing about a later day
decoded.not-measured: whether the truncation is by tokens of a named tokenizer or by some proxy for them; only bytes were measured, and the vendor's claim is about tokens. Whether maxTokenBudget affects microsoft_code_sample_search or microsoft_docs_fetch was not tested, and the vendor's wording says "search tool responses"
decoded.characters-and-bytes-are-equal-for-this-: a reviewer pointed out that Python's len(text) counts characters, not UTF-8 bytes, so a command written that way cannot verify a byte figure in general. Measured for this query at 12:40Z, a third reading: characters 28958 and UTF-8 bytes 28958 unbudgeted, 12675 and 12675 at maxTokenBudget=2000, 2341 and 2341 at 200, equal in every case, so this content is pure ASCII and the published figures are right read either way. The command counts len(text.encode()) regardless, because the next query need not be ASCII and a reader has to be measuring the same thing the record reports.

finding: The maxTokenBudget query parameter Microsoft documents on this MCP endpoint works for an anonymous caller and is measurable: one query, one pass, 28958 content bytes with no parameter (59003 raw), 12675 at maxTokenBudget=2000 (26155 raw) and 2341 at 200 (5310 raw). Two things the vendor does not state. The RESULT COUNT is ten at every budget, so the parameter truncates each chunk rather than returning fewer whole results, and an agent budgeting context cannot choose the other trade. And maxTokenBudget=0 and maxTokenBudget=notanumber are ignored silently, both returning the full unbudgeted response with no error: a bad value does not fail, it uncaps the response for a caller who believes it is capped. Only bytes were measured (UTF-8; for this query characters and bytes are equal at all three figures); the vendor's claim is about tokens and this record does not convert between them.

reproducibility.command: A='content-type: application/json';B='accept: application/json, text/event-stream';Q='{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":10,"method":"tools/call","params":{"name":"microsoft_docs_search","arguments":{"query":"Azure Functions durable orchestration"}}}';for q in '' '?maxTokenBudget=2000' '?maxTokenBudget=200' '?maxTokenBudget=0' '?maxTokenBudget=notanumber';do curl -s -X POST "https://learn.microsoft.com/api/mcp$q" -H "$A" -H "$B" -d "$Q" | sed -n 's/^data: //p' | python3 -c 'import json,sys;d=json.load(sys.stdin);t=d["result"]["content"][0]["text"];print(len(t.encode()),len(json.loads(t)["results"]))';done
